target.title: fix(signal): forward reply metadata for durable sends
target.body:
## Summary

Signal native replies now preserve quote metadata across durable delivery, direct outbound sends, queued recovery, and unknown-send reconciliation. Signal direct replies derive the native quote author from the normalized target, while group/durable replies carry inbound sender metadata when the reply still targets the current inbound message.

The PR also closes the retargeting edge cases around native replies: explicit `replyToId` beats inline reply directives, single-use implicit replies consume the id and author together, and payloads that retarget a different reply id do not inherit a stale ambient quote author.

## What Changed

- Signal send surfaces: message adapter text/media, formatted text/media, and attached-result text/media forward `replyToId` and `replyToAuthor` into Signal send options.
- Durable delivery and queue recovery: core send contexts, durable delivery, queue storage/replay, and unknown-send reconciliation preserve optional `replyToAuthor` alongside `replyToId`.
- Reply routing rules: explicit `replyToId` now wins over parsed inline `[[reply_to:...]]` directives, and ambient reply authors are cleared when the effective reply id no longer matches the original reply target.
- Plugin SDK contract: the outbound context API baseline hash is regenerated for the intentional optional `replyToAuthor` send-context field.

## Proof

Behavioral proof in the net diff:

- Direct Signal sends using `signal:u:Alice` normalize the send target and derived native quote author to `username:alice`.
- Durable Signal replies pass native quote metadata through message adapter, formatted, attached-result, queued recovery, and unknown-send reconciliation paths.
- Reconciled recovery commit hooks receive `replyToAuthor` when the effective reply id still matches the queued reply id, and omit it when recovery retargeted to a different effective reply id.
- Single-use reply mode suppresses both `replyToId` and `replyToAuthor` after the first low-level send.

Screenshots: not included because this is backend/channel delivery behavior with no human-visible UI surface changed.

## Verification

Reviewer-checkable behavior on rebased head `ed35bed2060`:

- `python3 /Users/jmerhi/repos/skills/skills/pr-proof-pack/scripts/pr_net_diff.py --markdown` reports base `origin/main 7e0324263b86`, head `ed35bed20603`, and no branch-only churn.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed.
- `corepack pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/send.test.ts extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts src/channels/turn/durable-delivery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts src/infra/outbound/delivery-queue.recovery.test.ts src/infra/outbound/message-action-runner.core-send.test.ts` passed locally after the rebase.
- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox `tbx_01kx08e8ana2z83cwhe4j7he6b` (`violet-krill`) passed the same focused Vitest command, `corepack pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check`, `corepack pnpm tsgo:core`, `corepack pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `corepack pnpm tsgo:extensions`, and `corepack pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`.

Review note: independent cold review found one recovery lifecycle gap around `replyToAuthor`; this head includes the production fix and regression coverage. Native Codex review was attempted repeatedly but the review service returned `429 Too Many Requests` before a verdict, so it is not listed as completed proof.
